extracted.intended_audience: federal agency procurement officials, contracting officers, and agency leadership responsible for implementing OMB Circular A-76
extracted.subtask_short: OMB A-76 implementation for C/I activities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for federal agencies on when and how to acquire commercial or industrial products and services (in-house vs contract), including required cost-comparison methods, approvals, inventories, review schedules, employee protections, and appeals procedures under OMB Circular A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Defense justification for in-house activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government commercial or industrial activity, operated by military personnel, may be justified when: (a) The activity or military personnel assigned are utilized in or subject to deployment in a direct combat support role; (b) The activity is essential for training in those skills which are exclusively military in nature; or (c) The activity is needed to provide appropriate work assignments for Career progression or a rotation base for overseas assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a non-economy justification allowing in-house operation when activities directly support military readiness/training or personnel management needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depot and intermediate maintenance special-justification
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government commercial or industrial activity providing depot or intermediate level maintenance may be justified in accordance with Criteria approved by the Secretary of Defense to ensure a ready and controlled source of technical competence and resources necessary to meet military contingencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification under these criteria must explain, case-by-case, why needed capability cannot be supplied by (a) a private commercial source; or (b) contract operation of Government-owned facilities. Such justification must be approved at the military department assistant secretary level or equivalent in the defense agencies. Criteria will limit in-house capability to the minimum necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy-based authorization: comparative cost analysis requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision for in-house performance based on economy must be supported by a comparative cost analysis prepared in accordance with this Circular and the supplementing Cost Comparison Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If comparative cost analysis indicates Government can provide the product or service at a lower total cost than private commercial source, in-house activity may be authorized. All cost-based decisions must follow the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rule — equal scope and performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Government and commercial cost figures must be based on the same scope of work and the same level of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires preparation of a sufficiently precise work statement with performance standards that can be monitored for either mode of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rule — use of standard cost factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard cost factors will be used as prescribed by the Cost Comparison Handbook and as supplemented by agencies for particular operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must defend any variations in costing from one case to another; follow prescribed standard factors unless justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rule — full cost accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons are to be aimed at full cost, to the maximum extent practical in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All significant Government costs (including allocation of overhead and indirect costs) must be considered, both for direct Government performance and for administration of a contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation design to prevent contractor 'buy-in'
rubrics_metrics.description: In solicitations for continuing workloads, solicitations should provide for prepriced options or renewal options for the out-years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepriced/renewal options guard against 'buy-in' pricing and provide advantages such as continuity of operation, potential lower prices when contractor provides equipment/facilities, and reduced turbulence. Use unless otherwise inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for conducting cost comparison studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, agencies should not conduct cost comparison studies to justify a Government commercial or industrial activity for products or services estimated to be less than $100,000 in annual operating costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities below this threshold should be performed by contract unless in-house performance is justified under other criteria. However, if inadequate competition or other factors make commercial prices unreasonable, a cost comparison may be conducted after reasonable efforts to obtain satisfactory commercial prices and sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity cost rate for capital and asset sale proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost comparison will use a rate of 10% per annum as the Opportunity cost of capital investments and of the net proceeds from the potential sale of capital assets, as prescribed in the Cost Comparison Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this prescribed rate in the comparative analysis unless the Handbook provides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract cost figure must be based on binding firm bids/proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: The contract cost figure must be based on a binding firm bid or proposal, solicited in accordance with pertinent acquisition regulations. Bidders or offerors must be told that an in-house cost estimate is being developed and that a contract may or may not result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures contractor figures are realistic and informed; contracting procedures must follow acquisition regs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government contract administration cost factor
rubrics_metrics.description: The factor to be used for the Government's cost of administering contracts, in addition to other costs of using contract performance as specified in the Handbook, is 4% of the contract price or expected cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include this 4% administration factor in contract-side cost estimates per the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government employee benefit and other cost factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Government cost factors to be used: retirement benefits 20.4% (dynamic normal cost projection for Civil Service Retirement Fund); insurance (life and health) benefits 3.7% (actual cost); workmen's compensation, bonuses and awards, and unemployment programs 1.9%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these prescribed percentages when calculating full government personnel costs in cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum savings thresholds for conversion decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: An existing in-house activity will not be converted to contract performance on the basis of economy unless it will result in savings of at least 10% of the estimated Government personnel costs for the period of the comparative analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a 'new start', approval on the basis of economy requires savings at least equal to 10% of Government personnel costs plus 25% of the cost of ownership of equipment and facilities for the analysis period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review of cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: All cost comparisons must be reviewed by an activity independent of the cost analysis preparation to ensure conformance to the instructions in the Cost Comparison Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An independent review body/activity must validate conformance and accuracy of comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency implementation responsibilities and designated officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will designate an official at the assistant secretary or equivalent level, and officials at subordinate contact points for major components, to have overall responsibility for implementation of this Circular within the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also establish one or more central offices as contact points with access to all decision documents and data pertinent to actions under the Circular; forward internal instructions to OFPP for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promulgation and OFPP notification timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 90 days after the date of issuance, each agency will promulgate this Circular, with the minimum necessary internal instructions, identifying the designated official and the central and subordinate contact points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of internal instructions and subsequent changes will be forwarded to the Office of Federal Procurement Policy for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract clauses and compliance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts awarded as a result of reviews under Circular A-76 must contain all applicable clauses and provisions related to equal employment opportunities, veterans' preference, and minimum wages and fringe benefits, including implementation of OFPP Policy Letter No. 78-2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with employment/compensation laws and OFPP policies in resulting contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of displaced Federal employees under resulting contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a provision, consistent with Government post employment conflict of interest standards, that the contractor will give Federal employees, displaced as a result of the conversion to contract performance, the right of first refusal for employment openings on the contract in positions for which they are qualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract language must provide displaced employees an employment opportunity with the contractor where qualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract award and performance monitoring standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts must be awarded to a responsible and responsive bidder or offeror, as required by applicable acquisition regulations, and are to be administered and monitored to achieve proper performance, using appropriate contractual remedies any time performance is less than satisfactory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow acquisition regs for responsibility/responsiveness and actively monitor contractor performance with remedies for deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency responsibilities toward displaced Federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will exert maximum effort to find suitable employment for any displaced Federal employees, including: (a) Giving them priority consideration for suitable positions with the Government; (b) Paying reasonable costs for training and relocation when these will contribute directly to placement; (c) Arranging for gradual transition when conversions are made to provide greater opportunity for attrition and placement; and (d) Coordinating with the Department of Labor and other agencies to obtain private sector employment for separated workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must take proactive personnel-placement and assistance measures when in-house work is converted to contract performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing changes in mode of performance aligned with budget process
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will provide for alterations to the mode of performance to be timed in consonance with, and adjusted for, the budget Process to the extent required and consistent with the firm bid cost study approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate timing of conversions/changes with agency budgeting and cost-study schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory requirements for commercial and industrial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will prepare and maintain a complete inventory of all individual commercial or industrial activities which they operate. The inventory should include for each activity: the amount of the Government's capital investment, the annual cost of operation, the date the activity was last reviewed, and the basis on which the activity is being continued under this Circular. The inventory will be updated at least annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventories provide transparency and tracking of activities subject to A-76 review; update annually to reflect review results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory requirements for potentially in-house-performable contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies will prepare and maintain an inventory of all contracts in excess of $100,000 annually (except those under authorized set-aside programs) for services which the agency determines could reasonably be performed in-house. The inventory will include: the contract number, name of the contractor, contract period, period of any options, and the total contract price or estimated cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory updates must reflect exercise of options and termination and award of contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review scheduling for activities and contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies will prepare a detailed schedule for the review of each commercial or industrial activity and contract in the inventory to determine if existing performance continues to be in accordance with the policy and guidelines of this Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule reviews of in-house activities during the three-year period following issuance; consider non-cost criteria first; if not justified under non-cost criteria, conduct cost comparison. For contracts, schedule must show contract expiry and review dates. Schedules to be provided to OFPP within 120 days, made available to affected employees/representatives and contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review frequency and waiver rules
rubrics_metrics.description: After the initial review, activities approved for continuation will be reviewed again at least once every five years. When agency head or designee determines circumstances supporting initial approval are not subject to change, subsequent reviews may be waived; the activity remains in inventory and waiver/justification will be made available upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides periodic reassessment but allows waiver where conditions are stable; documentation must be accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension relief for agencies with excessive review load
rubrics_metrics.description: When the number of commercial and industrial activities and the number of covered contracts is so great that reviews cannot be completed in the prescribed time period, the agency may request approval from the Office of Federal Procurement Policy, OMB, to schedule the reviews over a longer period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may petition OFPP/OMB for schedule relief when workload makes original schedule impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: New start approval and timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A new start should not be initiated by an executive agency unless the justification for establishing the activity under the provisions of this Circular has been reviewed and approved by a senior official of the agency. A new start which involves a capital investment or annual costs of $500,000 or more must be approved by the agency head or by an official at the assistant secretary or equivalent level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions to implement Circular should normally be completed before the agency's budget request is submitted to OMB; where long lead times exist, comparative cost analysis may be delayed for acquisition lead time but final determination must follow Circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of contract operation before Government ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: When Government ownership of facilities is necessary, the possibility of contract operation must be considered before in-house performance is approved as a new start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If justification for Government operation depends on relative cost, comparative cost analysis may be delayed to accommodate facility lead times; but contract operation must be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: When comparative cost analysis may be omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: When in-house performance to meet a new requirement is not feasible, or when contract performance would be under an authorized set-aside program, a contract can be awarded without conducting a comparative cost analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set-aside awards and situations where in-house performance infeasible are exceptions to the cost-comparison requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set-aside program treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts awarded under authorized set-aside programs will not be reviewed for possible in-house performance. New requirements suitable for award under a set-aside program should be satisfied by such a contract without a comparative cost analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversely, in-house activities (in excess of $100,000 annually) will not be considered for performance under a set-aside contract except when the conversion is justified by a comparative cost analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals procedure — scope and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will establish a procedure for an informal administrative review of determinations made under this Circular. This procedure will only be used to resolve questions of the determination between contract and in-house performance. The appeals procedure will provide for an independent, objective review and an expeditious determination, within 30 days, made by an official at the same or higher level than the official who approved the original decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are an internal administrative safeguard; they do not authorize appeal outside the agency or judicial review. Procedure and determinations may not be subject to negotiation, arbitration, or agreements with any one party. Agency appeal procedures must be submitted to OFPP for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for affected parties during appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal procedure is intended to protect Federal employees and their representative organizations, contractors and potential contractors, and contract employees and their representatives; the procedure and agency determinations may not be subject to negotiation, arbitration, or agreements with any one of those parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency decisions are final after the internal appeal; appeals do not create external or judicial remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and transitional provision
rubrics_metrics.description: This Circular is effective May 1, 1979, but need not be applied to studies in process where a solicitation for contract bids or proposals was issued prior to the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New rules apply from effective date but do not retroactively disturb ongoing solicitations issued before that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of commercial and industrial activities (definitional guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment A: lists examples of commercial and industrial activities such as audiovisual products and services, automatic data processing, maintenance/overhaul/repair (aircraft, ships, vehicles, electronic equipment, weapons), systems engineering/installation/operation/maintenance (communications, radar, satellite tracking), manufacturing/fabrication/processing, real property construction and maintenance, industrial shops and services, health services, transportation, printing and reproduction, research and development, office services, security, food services, laundry/library/mapping/training/utility operation, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this illustrative list to identify activities subject to the Circular; the list is non-exhaustive but shows typical functions considered commercial/industrial.
